enumeration.method: Five uncommented Theorem environments before the appendix command in the matching-version TeX; corroborated by main-section HTML and checked against printed PDF labels and complete statements. The main article and references end on page 25; Supplementary Material begins on page 26.
enumeration.boundary_probe_note: The acquisition boundary probe initially emitted a short portion of supplementary page 27 after detecting the boundary on page 26. That output was excluded from extraction and was not used to resolve any definition or theorem.

checks: The independent five-Theorem inventory was source-checked and validated before interface extraction.
The finalizer derived canonical dependencies and same-paper paths; a separate validator process accepted the completed census against its hash-pinned inventory.
All 27 source passages were compared with the main-text PDF, including Algorithm 2 and the four complete numbered Assumptions.
Every highlight selector was checked for a source-backed literal match, with at least one match in each original source passage or source label.

Every derived theorem path was reviewed. Gaussian comparison proof tools were not added as statement dependencies of the FDR results; model-specific bootstrap and signal members retained their separate paths.

source_notes: The source is arXiv:2108.09904v2 (15 September 2023), pinned independently of the 2024 publisher version. No identity of numbering across versions is asserted.
Theorem 6.3 prints FDP in both conclusions. Both the PDF and TeX support that transcription; the second occurrence has not been changed to FDR.

Theorem 3.1 uses the centered Gaussian pair fixed above it; the main-text theorem does not separately state variance lower bounds. The variance dependence discussed in Remark 3.2 is not silently inserted as a new theorem hypothesis.
Theorem 3.3 locally binds the common disjoint covariance-block partition and its count. That count is not conflated with the connected-component count of the tested graph in Section 5.
Section 2.1 excludes the diagonal in its degree-testing vector, but Section 5 prints the full row norm in the null-node set. Both original passages are retained.

Section 4 defines a row-wise response-selection problem and maximum row sparsity, then uses the word columns in a nearby sentence. The source wording is preserved without resolving that inconsistency by rewriting it.

The source applies Algorithm 2 to a rectangular multitask input, although its printed loop and order statistics use a square-graph index set excluding the diagonal. The adaptation is not expanded into an invented algorithm.
The uncentered T_E in (2.2) and centered estimation-error T_E in Section 6 are preserved as separate source usages.

The Gaussian-model dependence set (5.3) and the general influence-covariance set in Section 6 have different predicates. In particular, the general set does not inherit k1!=k2 or the full precision-pattern constraints.
Assumption 6.2 omits the component-count divisor p used in Assumption 5.1; it also includes zeta2*d^4. Both distinctions are preserved.
The displayed multiplier statistic (5.2) uses the initial precision estimate, rather than the standardized one-step estimate that is passed to Algorithm 2.

The complete general approximation assumption retains the nested conditional probability bound, uniform quantification over edge sets, independent normal multipliers, variance lower bound and both psi1 moment bounds.

review_limits: This audit preserves and resolves main-text statements; it does not certify their proofs or silently correct source inconsistencies.
Supplementary definitions, proofs and refinements were excluded. Unknown main-text conventions remain explicitly unresolved.
